description:
Execute a read-only SQL query. Allowed statements: SELECT, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN.

<usecase>
Use when:
- Querying data from tables (SELECT with WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, etc.)
- Aggregations: COUNT, SUM, AVG, GROUP BY, HAVING
- Listing server variables or status (SHOW)
- Viewing table structure (DESCRIBE)
</usecase>

<when_not_to_use>
- Data changes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) → use writeQuery (not available in read-only mode)
- Query performance analysis → use explainQuery
- Discovering tables or columns → use listTables (pass detailed=true for column-level metadata)
- Switching database context (USE is rejected) → pass the `database` argument
</when_not_to_use>

<examples>
✓ "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = 'active'"
✓ "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY region"
✓ "SHOW TABLES" or "DESCRIBE users"
✗ "INSERT INTO users ..." → use writeQuery (not available in read-only mode)
✗ "EXPLAIN SELECT ..." → use explainQuery for structured analysis
</examples>

<what_it_returns>
A JSON array of row objects, each keyed by column name.

Long string values are cut and end in `…[truncated, N chars total]`; read the rest with `SUBSTRING`/`SUBSTR`. Rows past the response size cap are dropped: a `SELECT` page ends early and `nextCursor` resumes at the first row left out, while other statements report the count in `rowsOmitted`. When either happens the response carries `truncated: true` and a `hint`.
</what_it_returns>

<pagination>
`SELECT` results are paginated. Pass the prior response's `nextCursor` as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Order by a unique key so pages neither skip nor repeat rows. Pages stay within the statement's own `LIMIT` and `OFFSET`. Write a row limit as a literal `LIMIT n`: other forms (`FETCH FIRST`, expressions) make every page read the whole result. `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`, and `EXPLAIN` return a single page and ignore `cursor`.
</pagination>

<timeout>
Each call stops at the configured query timeout. On a timeout, check the plan with explainQuery before retrying: filter on indexed columns, or limit inner result sets before joining or aggregating. For a query known to be slow, pass `timeout` (seconds, at least 1) to allow more time. This only helps if the server allows a higher maximum, which is often the same as the default; a value above it is rejected with an error naming the maximum.
</timeout>

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's `nextCursor`; omit for the first page.

database.description: Database to run the query against. Defaults to the active database.

timeout.description: Seconds this call may run, from 1 up to the server maximum. Defaults to the configured query timeout.

name: readQuery

hint.description: How to fetch less data; present only when `truncated` is `true`.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor pointing to the next page. Absent when this is the final
page, when the result fits in one page, or when the statement is a
non-`SELECT` kind that does not paginate (e.g. `SHOW`, `EXPLAIN`).

rows.description: Result rows, each a JSON object keyed by a column name.

rowsOmitted.description: Rows the response cap dropped that no cursor can fetch again.

truncated.description: Present and `true` when a character cap cut a value or dropped rows.

title: Read Query
